note: Derived setting packs (lane STYLEGEN-1, docs/STYLEGEN-PLAN.md section 2). The create flow reads this table only when its tag-scored pack choice would refuse the brief (no pack with room patterns covers the genre) or would pick a pack that does not cover the genre at all. Rows match the BRIEF (setting.genre, then words of setting.place, build_types, props and unrecognised), never the prompt text; the first matching row wins. Each reference is tried in order: a reference without room patterns is skipped, a mood the existing derivation refuses (tools.mood_pack.derive_all: kits/core/mood.py checks, unchanged) falls through to the next reference with a report line, and no usable reference keeps the honest refusal. A derived pack keeps its reference's style-gate and N64 thresholds (only accent_hues may differ, by the derivation's own check). brief_cues are applied by the keyword (no-model) brief only: a cue word of the prompt sets the brief's place when the brief's genre is listed and its place is still the genre default. A row marked prefer (STYLEGEN-2) is also asked when the tag-scored choice succeeds: its reference wins over that pick when it can be used (the pick is kept, with the setting lines, when it cannot). A reference without a mood is used as shipped (no derivation, nothing installed).

emissive_margin.note: STYLEGEN-2: a derived setting pack keeps the mood's neon margin (saturation below .55 or value below .88) for every palette colour an emissive role paints, as DRAWN in the look profiles of the setting's rooms (role emission, unlit level and the profile grade on top of the palette colour). Only OKLCh chroma is lowered; the result passes the unchanged mood checks again (create_setting.emissive_margin, tools.mood_pack.derive_all adjust). The N64 gate's neon threshold is not touched.

settings.why: a pale, cold planet surface with a station interior: the planet terrain kit under the alien_world exterior light (its calibrated horizon haze), recoloured; station pieces built in the same palette
a space station interior (STYLEGEN-2): the station kit used as shipped, on its own calibrated rooms (the SCIFIKIT hangar and bridge)
a sea-floor station: the planet terrain kit and the station kit, recoloured deep sea

jungle temple ruins (STYLEGEN-2): the ancient kit's overgrown court and sanctum in the jungle_temple look, used as shipped (ANCIENTKIT calibrated it on these plans). Preferred: a jungle brief the tag-scored choice does not refuse lands on a medieval castle (another family's look)
an ancient temple (STYLEGEN-2): the ancient kit's sun road and sanctum in the ancient_ruins look, used as shipped. Preferred: the tag-scored choice lands on a medieval castle (another family's look)

a desert (STYLEGEN-2): the ancient kit's sun road and sanctum in the ancient_ruins look (the shipped desert look), used as shipped. Preferred: the tag-scored choice scores library tags and lands on a western frontier town (another family's look). No setting words: the keyword brief gives every desert brief the same default build types, so words would not separate them, and a model brief must route the same way

settings.entry_camera_why: STYLEGEN-2 G2: the plaza camera sees only the low, pastel cloud band of the candy sky (flat sky 0.039 < 0.06 on the first view, STYLEGEN-1 and STYLEGEN-2 runs); the plaza's own look_up_wide alternate (look-at +0.8 m, fov 66, inside camera_knobs) measured 0.149 on the same pack. No look profile could change it: the derived pack's three exterior profiles carry the same sky, fog and grade
settings.why: a storybook castle in candy pastels: the medieval kit recoloured with the candy_pastel mood
